title: Construction 17: Incentre and incircle of a triangle (straight edge and compass)
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle with angle bisectors meeting at the incentre and the incircle touching the sides, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the incircle of the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 8$ cm, $|BC| = 7$ cm and $|AC| = 5$ cm. Show all construction lines.
example.final: incircle with centre $I$, the meeting point of the angle bisectors

steps.say: Draw $[AB]$ first. Then find $C$ with two arcs, so the sides are accurate.

rows.aside: Draw $[AB]$ with $|AB| = 8$ cm.
With the compass point on $A$, draw an arc of radius $5$ cm.
With the compass point on $B$, draw an arc of radius $7$ cm. Where the arcs cross is $C$.
Join $A$ to $C$ and $B$ to $C$.

steps.say: The incentre lies on each angle bisector. Bisect the angle at $A$ using Construction 1.

rows.aside: With the compass point on $A$, draw an arc that cuts $[AB]$ and $[AC]$.
Keep the same width. Put the point on each cut in turn and draw two arcs that cross inside the angle.
Draw a line from $A$ through the crossing point.

steps.say: Do the same at $B$. The two bisectors meet at one point, the **incentre** $I$.

rows.aside: Repeat the construction at $B$.
Label the point where the two bisectors cross $I$.
Two bisectors are enough. Leave all the arcs showing.

steps.say: The circle must touch each side, so its radius is the shortest distance from $I$ to a side. Drop a perpendicular.

rows.aside: From $I$, construct the perpendicular to $[AB]$ (Construction 5). Where it meets $[AB]$ is $T$.
With the compass point on $I$ and the pencil on $T$, draw the circle.
It touches all three sides.

title: Construction 19: Tangent to a circle at a given point on it
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: circle centre O with P on it, the radius OP and the tangent perpendicular at P, with arcs left visible

example.question: A circle has centre $O$ and radius $4$ cm. $P$ is a point on the circle. Construct the tangent to the circle at $P$.

steps.say: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at $P$. Draw the radius first.

rows.aside: Draw the circle with centre $O$ and radius $4$ cm. Mark $P$ on it.
Draw the line from $O$ through $P$, and extend it past $P$.

steps.say: Construction 4 draws a perpendicular to a line through a point on it. First mark two points the same distance from $P$.

rows.aside: With the compass point on $P$, draw an arc that cuts the extended radius on both sides of $P$.
Call the two cuts $X$ and $Y$. Now $|PX| = |PY|$.

steps.say: Open the compass wider. Draw two arcs that cross above and below the line.

rows.aside: With the compass point on $X$, draw an arc above the line and one below it.
Keep the same width. With the point on $Y$, draw arcs that cross the first two.
Mark the crossing points $U$ and $V$.

steps.say: Join $U$ and $V$. This line passes through $P$ at a right angle to $[OP]$, so it is the **tangent**.

rows.aside: With the straight edge, draw the line $UV$ through $P$.
Label it $t$. It touches the circle at $P$ only.

title: Construction 21: Centroid of a triangle
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle A(1,2) B(7,4) C(4,9) on a grid with midpoint D of BC and the median, with arcs left visible

example.question: The triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1, 2)$, $B(7, 4)$ and $C(4, 9)$. Find the midpoint $D$ of $[BC]$, then find the centroid $G$ of the triangle.

steps.say: A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. Average the coordinates of $B$ and $C$ to find $\hl{1}{D}$.

rows.aside: So $\hl{1}{D} = \left(\frac{11}{2}, \frac{13}{2}\right)$. The median is $[AD]$.

steps.say: The centroid $\hl{2}{G}$ is two thirds of the way from $A$ to $D$. Find the $x$-coordinate first.
Do the same with the $y$-values.
A quick check: the centroid is the average of the three vertices.

rows.aside: Both methods agree. $\hl{2}{G} = (4, 5)$.

title: Construction 7: Divide a segment into any number of equal parts without measuring
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: segment AB divided into three equal parts using a ray with equal steps, with arcs left visible

example.question: Divide the segment $[AB]$ into three equal parts, using only a compass and straight edge.

steps.say: From $A$, draw a ray at any angle to $[AB]$. Make it long enough to hold three equal steps.

rows.aside: Any angle works. It only has to be a different direction from $[AB]$.

steps.say: Set the compass to any small width. Put the point on $A$ and mark $C_1$ on the ray. Keep the width. Move to $C_1$ and mark $C_2$. Move to $C_2$ and mark $C_3$.

rows.aside: Do not change the compass width between marks, so $|AC_1| = |C_1C_2| = |C_2C_3|$.

steps.say: With the ruler, join $C_3$ to $B$.

rows.aside: This line is the one the others will be parallel to.

steps.say: Copy the angle at $C_3$ up to $C_2$ and $C_1$ with the compass. Draw a line through $C_2$ parallel to $C_3B$, meeting $[AB]$ at $D_2$. Draw another through $C_1$, meeting $[AB]$ at $D_1$.

rows.aside: Leave all arcs and lines on the page. They are the construction lines.

steps.say: The parallels cut equal pieces on both lines, so the three pieces on $[AB]$ are equal.

title: Construction 22: Orthocentre of a triangle
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: triangle with its three altitudes meeting at the orthocentre, with arcs left visible

example.question: Construct the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $C$. Draw an arc that cuts $[AB]$ at two points. From each of those points, draw an arc below $[AB]$ with the same width. Join $C$ to where the arcs cross.

rows.aside: This is Construction 3: a perpendicular to a line through a point not on it.

steps.say: Repeat from $A$ on the side $[BC]$. Extend $[BC]$ if the arcs cannot reach it. Join $A$ to where the arcs cross.

rows.aside: Each altitude meets its side at $90^\circ$.

steps.say: The two altitudes cross at one point. Label it $H$.

rows.aside: Two correct altitudes that do not cross earn only part of the marks. Extend them until they meet.

steps.say: Draw the altitude from $B$ to $[AC]$ in the same way. It should pass through $H$.

rows.aside: If it misses $H$, one of the arcs was drawn with a changed compass width.

title: Derive formula 2: the sine rule
show: triangle ABC with sides a,b,c, height h from B to AC and the area expressions marked

example.question: In triangle $ABC$ the sides opposite $A$, $B$ and $C$ are $a$, $b$ and $c$. Using area $=\tfrac12 ab\sin C$, prove that $\dfrac{a}{\sin A}=\dfrac{b}{\sin B}=\dfrac{c}{\sin C}$.

steps.say: The area formula works from any vertex: take two sides and the angle between them. Do it at $A$, at $B$ and at $C$.

rows.aside: All three are the area of the same triangle, so they are equal.

steps.say: Divide every form of the area by $\tfrac12 abc$. In each one two letters cancel and a single $\sin$ over a side is left.
The three areas are equal, so the three results are equal. Turn each fraction upside down to get the form in the tables.
